lessons.title: Supabase Architecture Overview
lessons.content:
# Supabase Architecture Overview

Supabase is an open-source backend platform built around Postgres, authentication, storage, realtime, and edge functions.

### Key idea
Unlike document-first platforms, Supabase starts from a relational database model.

### Main services
- Postgres database
- Auth
- Storage
- Realtime subscriptions
- Edge Functions

### Practical takeaway
Designing tables, constraints, and policies well matters more in Supabase than trying to hide database structure behind vague application code.

lessons.title: Project Setup and API Keys
lessons.content:
# Project Setup and API Keys

A Supabase project exposes a URL plus API keys used by clients and servers.

### Important distinction
- The anonymous key is safe for client-side use when paired with Row Level Security.
- Service role keys are server-only and must never be exposed in the browser.

### Setup rule
Create separate client helpers for browser and server code so the wrong credentials do not leak across boundaries.

lessons.title: Working with Tables and Rows
lessons.content:
# Working with Tables and Rows

Supabase queries are built on top of PostgREST, so you interact with tables in a relational way.

### Common operations
- `select()` reads rows.
- `insert()` creates rows.
- `update()` changes rows.
- `delete()` removes rows.

### Schema tip
Use foreign keys, unique constraints, and sensible column names early. They improve both correctness and query clarity.

lessons.title: Authentication and Sessions
lessons.content:
# Authentication and Sessions

Supabase Auth supports email/password, magic links, OAuth providers, and session handling.

### Workflow basics
- Sign up or sign in a user.
- Read the current session.
- React to auth state changes.
- Use the access token on the client or server where appropriate.

### Operational rule
Treat session refresh and logout flows as first-class behavior, not edge cases, especially in multi-tab web apps.

lessons.title: Filtering, Joins, and Pagination
lessons.content:
# Filtering, Joins, and Pagination

Supabase query builders support filtering and selecting related data through Postgres relationships.

### Typical patterns
- Use `.eq()`, `.ilike()`, `.in()`, and range filters.
- Select related rows using foreign key relationships.
- Paginate long lists instead of loading everything.

### Design note
Search UIs should decide whether they need prefix matching, fuzzy search, or full-text search. A plain substring filter is often not enough for production data.

lessons.title: Realtime Channels
lessons.content:
# Realtime Channels

Supabase Realtime can broadcast database changes or custom events to connected clients.

### Good use cases
- Activity feeds
- Presence indicators
- Collaborative dashboards
- Admin monitoring tools

### Caution
Use realtime intentionally. If every table change becomes a live client subscription, performance and debugging get messy quickly.

lessons.title: Row Level Security Fundamentals
lessons.content:
# Row Level Security Fundamentals

Row Level Security, usually called RLS, is the main access-control mechanism in Supabase.

### Why it matters
RLS policies decide which rows a user can select, insert, update, or delete.

### Core rule
Enable RLS for exposed tables and write explicit policies for each operation that should be allowed.

### Review habit
Test both positive and negative policy paths. A policy that works for owners but fails for admins, or vice versa, is a common production bug.

lessons.title: Storage Buckets and File Policies
lessons.content:
# Storage Buckets and File Policies

Supabase Storage provides buckets for file uploads along with policies to control access.

### Common flow
- Create a bucket.
- Upload files with a predictable path convention.
- Use signed URLs or public URLs based on the use case.
- Protect private files with storage policies.

### Practical rule
File path structure should reflect ownership or tenancy, otherwise authorization becomes harder to reason about.

lessons.title: Edge Functions and Server Work
lessons.content:
# Edge Functions and Server Work

Supabase Edge Functions run backend logic close to users and are useful for webhooks, secure mutations, and integrations.

### Use them for
- Secret-dependent integrations
- Payment or email workflows
- Controlled admin actions
- Request validation before database writes

### Engineering guideline
Keep functions narrow. One function with a clear input and output is easier to secure and deploy than a generic catch-all endpoint.
